scope: Re-test of all 23 findings from run 2026-09-22T222029Z against the working tree (useDialogFocus, modal, board, title bar and login changes). Then new checks, all headless. Keyboard-only walk in Chromium and Firefox: login (failure uses a throwaway username), board Tab order, Create/Edit/Delete-confirm traps (12 x Tab and 12 x Shift+Tab each), Escape, Close X, validation, the Severity select, save, search and Clear, open a row with Enter and Space, edit twice, close a bug from Edit, delete with confirm and cancel, injected 500s on POST/PUT/DELETE, the Open/Closed toggle, sort headers, logout. ariaSnapshot of every view in both engines; status-region mutations recorded with a MutationObserver; contrast computed from getComputedStyle (26 pairs); reflow at 320x256, 320x640 and 640x900 in both engines; table keyboard scroll at 320; 1.4.12 text spacing; forced-colors emulation; target sizes. Scoped run of tests/accessibility/ (Chromium, 12/12 passed). Every [a11y] bug created was deleted; none remain.
commands: curl -s localhost:5173/api/bugs (checked that no [a11y] bugs remain)

findings.title: Specs contain no accessibility requirement
findings.requirement: specs/design/theme.md 'Other UI/UX' (accessibility placeholder); WCAG 2.2 AA used as authority
findings.evidence: Re-tested: specs/design/theme.md:20 is still the placeholder; no WCAG or accessibility clause anywhere in specs/. tests/accessibility/ now guards 12 behaviours, but they encode fixes, not a stated requirement.
findings.fix: Add an accessibility section to theme.md committing to WCAG 2.2 AA (contrast, focus management in modals, keyboard operation, reflow at 320px) and an a11y acceptance criterion per feature.

findings.title: Search input has role="search", so it is exposed as a landmark, not a textbox
findings.requirement: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; 1.3.1 Info and Relationships
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. Header snapshot: `search` landmark containing `textbox "Search bugs by title"` (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/chromium/aria/03-board.yml, firefox same). Guarded by accessibility.spec.ts:28 (passed).
findings.repro: Log in, run page.locator('header').ariaSnapshot(); the input appears as `search`, not `textbox`/`searchbox`.
findings.fix: Remove role="search" from the <input>, use type="search" (searchbox role), and put role="search" on the wrapping <div>.

findings.title: Bug table rows have role="button", destroying row semantics
findings.requirement: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships; 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. Rows are `row` with `cell` children; the title cell holds `button "<title>"` (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/chromium/aria/03-board.yml). Enter and Space on the title button open Edit in Chromium and Firefox. Guarded by accessibility.spec.ts:10 and :33 (see a11y-27 on how weak :33 is).
findings.repro: Log in; page.getByRole('table').ariaSnapshot() -> rows listed as button.
findings.fix: Remove role/tabIndex/onKeyDown from <tr>; render the Title (or ID) cell content as a <button> that calls handleRowClick; keep the <tr> onClick for mouse users.

findings.title: Open/Closed toggle selected state is conveyed only visually
findings.requirement: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; 1.4.1 Use of Color
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. After Space on Closed: aria-pressed Open=false Closed=true in Chromium and Firefox (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/*/keyboard-path.log). Only the initial Open=true is guarded (accessibility.spec.ts:41).
findings.repro: Tab to Closed, press Space, read getAttribute('aria-pressed') on both buttons.
findings.fix: Add aria-pressed={stateFilter === "OPEN"} and aria-pressed={stateFilter === "CLOSED"} to the two buttons.

findings.title: Create and Edit modals do not trap focus; Tab walks into the page behind
findings.requirement: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order; 2.1.2 (aria-modal="true" contract); theme.md modal consistency
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. 12 x Tab and 12 x Shift+Tab never left the Create, Edit or Delete-confirm dialog in Chromium or Firefox; focus wraps Save -> Close -> Title (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/chromium/keyboard-path.log, firefox same).
findings.repro: Open New Bug with Enter, press Tab 7 times, check document.activeElement.closest('[role=dialog]') is null.
findings.fix: Use native <dialog>.showModal(), or set `inert` on #root content while a modal is open, or add a Tab/Shift+Tab wrap handler on the panel.

findings.title: Focus is dropped to <body> after closing a modal, saving, deleting, or clearing search
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. Focus returns to New Bug after Escape, Close X and Save (create); to the row title button after Escape and Save (edit); to the search input after Clear; to the h1 after delete and after a save that moves the row out of the Open view; to Username after Logout. Both engines (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/*/keyboard-path.log). Failure paths are a11y-24.
findings.repro: Focus New Bug, Enter, Escape; document.activeElement === document.body.
findings.fix: Store the trigger element when opening and call .focus() on it in onClose (New Bug, or the row's button); after delete focus the table or next row; after Clear search focus the search input.

findings.title: Delete confirmation dialog does not receive focus; focus stays behind it in the Edit dialog
findings.requirement: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order; 4.1.2 (two simultaneous aria-modal dialogs)
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. Enter on Delete focuses the confirm dialog Cancel; the Edit dialog gets aria-hidden=true and drops out of the tree (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/chromium/aria/07-confirm-delete.yml); Tab cycles Cancel/Delete/Close only; Escape returns focus to Delete. Both engines.
findings.repro: Open a bug, focus Delete, press Enter, read document.activeElement.
findings.fix: Focus the confirm dialog's Cancel button when showConfirmDelete becomes true, make the Edit dialog inert while it is shown, and return focus to Delete on cancel.

findings.title: Severity badge text fails 4.5:1 on its own tint (HIGH 3.77, MID 2.93, LOW 4.32)
findings.evidence: Re-measured from computed styles, unchanged (colours deliberately left as spec 08 tokens): HIGH #b84a2e on #efd7d1 3.77:1 (3.66 hovered); MID #a67c47 on #ebe2d7 2.93:1 (2.85); LOW #4a6b5e on #d7dedc 4.32:1 (4.20). Same colours on the Severity <select> in both modals. quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/contrast.txt. Nothing in the suite guards contrast.
findings.fix: Darken the text colours (e.g. HIGH #a24128, MID #7e5e36, LOW #47675a reach ~4.6:1 on white rows; go slightly darker for hovered rows) or lighten the tint; update spec 08 hex values to match.

findings.title: Login 'Log in' subtitle in #b8ae76 on white is 2.25:1
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. "Log in" is now an h2 in stone-600 #57534e on white: 7.63:1 (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/contrast.txt).
findings.fix: Use text-stone-700, or add a darker brand shade for text (e.g. #7a7040, 4.98:1).

findings.title: Search placeholder text is 2.41:1
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. Placeholder computed #78716c: 4.59:1 on stone-50, 4.80:1 on white (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/contrast.txt).
findings.fix: placeholder-stone-500 (#78716c: 4.59:1 on stone-50).

findings.title: Cancel buttons keep a stone-400 focus ring at 2.52:1
findings.requirement: WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (2.4.7 relies on it)
findings.evidence: Mostly fixed: rings on Login, inputs, New Bug, row buttons, toggle, Save measure #57534e 7.63:1; input borders #78716c 4.80:1; the selected toggle now has a stone-800 underline at 6.76:1 on its fill. Still failing: the three Cancel buttons (Create, Edit, Delete confirm) use focus:ring-stone-400, #a8a29e on white = 2.52:1. The confirm dialog now puts initial focus on that Cancel, so the first focus a keyboard user sees there is the faint one (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/chromium/screenshots/07c-confirm-cancel-focus-crop.png, quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/contrast.txt).
findings.fix: focus:ring-stone-600 on the three Cancel buttons.

findings.title: Board header does not reflow at 320 CSS px (400% zoom); Logout is off-screen
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. At 320x640 and 320x256, /board scrollWidth = clientWidth = 320 in Chromium and Firefox; header wraps: search 17-271 px, New Bug 29-129, Logout 154-240 (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/chromium/visual.log, quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/chromium/screenshots/10b-table-320-after-tab.png). The table itself is a11y-25.
findings.repro: Open /board with viewport 320x640 and compare document.documentElement.scrollWidth to clientWidth.
findings.fix: Add flex-wrap to the header, drop flex-shrink-0 on the button group, and make the search w-full below sm (e.g. `w-full sm:w-80`).

findings.title: Clear-search button is 22x36 px, next to the input
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. Clear search is 32x32 px (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/chromium/visual.log). Modal Close is 18x32 but has no adjacent target (passes on spacing).
findings.fix: p-2 or min-w-6 min-h-6 on the clear button (and on the Close X for consistency).

findings.title: Submitting login drops focus to <body> because the fields are disabled while loading
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. Wrong password with a throwaway username: focus stays in Username; both fields aria-invalid=true, aria-describedby=login-error; Chromium and Firefox. Guarded by tests/accessibility/login.spec.ts:7.
findings.repro: On /login type a bad password, press Enter, read document.activeElement.
findings.fix: Use readOnly/aria-disabled instead of disabled during submit, or focus the username field when setting error; add aria-invalid and aria-describedby pointing at the error.

findings.title: Page title is 'BuggyBoard' on every route
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. "Log in – BuggyBoard" on /login, "Board – BuggyBoard" on /board, both engines. Guarded by login.spec.ts:17.
findings.fix: Set document.title per route, e.g. 'Log in - BuggyBoard' and 'Board - BuggyBoard'.

findings.title: Login page has no main landmark and 'Log in' is a paragraph, not a heading
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. /login tree: `main` > heading level 1 "BuggyBoard", heading level 2 "Log in" (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/chromium/aria/01-login.yml).
findings.fix: Wrap the card in <main> and make 'Log in' an <h2> (or wrap it in a labelled <form>).

findings.title: No status live region: search results, filter, save and delete are not announced
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. A polite role=status region announces load ("15 open bugs shown."), search, filter ("1 closed bug shown."), create, save and delete ("Bug deleted. No bugs matched."), recorded with a MutationObserver in both engines (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/*/keyboard-path.log "[status changes"). Remaining defects are a11y-26.
findings.fix: Add a visually hidden role=status region announcing e.g. 'Sorted by Title ascending', 'Showing 3 closed bugs', 'Bug saved'.

findings.title: Open/Closed selected state disappears in forced-colors (Windows High Contrast) mode
findings.requirement: WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast; 1.4.1 Use of Color
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. Forced-colors emulation: the selected button keeps an underline (text-decoration underline) and the other has none; screenshots differ (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/chromium/screenshots/14-forced-colors-selected-Open.png, -Closed.png).
findings.fix: aria-pressed (a11y-04) plus a forced-colors-safe indicator on the selected button, e.g. a 2px border/underline, or `forced-colors:outline` on the selected one.

findings.title: Escape meant for a native <select> popup closes the whole Create/Edit modal and discards input
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. Headless Chromium and Firefox: ArrowDown then Escape on the focused Severity select leaves the Create dialog open with the typed title kept. Guarded by accessibility.spec.ts:62 (that test presses Escape on the select without opening it, so it covers the tagName guard, not a real open popup). Headed native popups still need a manual check.
findings.repro: BROWSER=chromium node quality-reports/2026-09-22T222029Z/evidence/a11y/walk.cjs; grep 'CLOSED the Create dialog' quality-reports/2026-09-22T222029Z/evidence/a11y/chromium/keyboard-path.log
findings.fix: In the Escape handler, return early if (e.target as HTMLElement).tagName === 'SELECT' or e.defaultPrevented; optionally confirm before discarding a dirty form.

findings.title: Edit modal gives no error for a blank field; Save just becomes disabled
findings.requirement: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships; 3.3.1 Error Identification
findings.evidence: Create is fixed: an empty submit sets aria-invalid=true and aria-describedby=create-bug-errors on Title and Description. Edit still reproduces: clearing Title leaves aria-invalid=null, no alert, and Save disabled, so Tab skips from Cancel to Close and nothing says why (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/edit-errors.txt).
findings.fix: Keep Save enabled and run validate() on submit (the error list is already rendered), or render a hint tied to the blank field with aria-invalid and aria-describedby.

findings.title: 'BuggyBoard' heading collapses to 0 px at 640 CSS px (200% zoom)
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. At 640x900 the h1 spans x 78-251 and is visible (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/chromium/visual.log).
findings.repro: Open /board at a 640 px wide viewport; header h1 getBoundingClientRect().width === 0.
findings.fix: Give the h1 min-w-fit or shrink-0 and let the header wrap (same change as a11y-12).

findings.title: Route changes (login -> board, logout -> login) are silent and leave focus on <body>
findings.requirement: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order; 4.1.3 (best practice for SPAs)
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. Login -> board moves focus to the h1 "BuggyBoard" and sets "Board – BuggyBoard"; Logout -> focus on Username and "Log in – BuggyBoard". Both engines.
findings.repro: grep -n 'Enter with correct password\|Focus on /login after logout' quality-reports/2026-09-22T222029Z/evidence/a11y/*/keyboard-path.log
findings.fix: On route change, set document.title and move focus to the page h1 (tabIndex=-1) or the username field.

findings.title: Firefox: table scroll container is an unnamed Tab stop
findings.evidence: Re-tested this run, no longer reproduces. The scroll wrapper is now `region "Bug table"`. In Firefox it is no longer a Tab stop at 1280 or 320 px (Owner header -> first row button). Its keyboard-scroll gap is a11y-25.
findings.fix: Add role="region" aria-label="Bugs table" tabIndex={0} to the wrapper so the stop is named, keyboard scrolling works in every engine, and Firefox users are not left guessing.

findings.title: A failed Create or Edit save drops focus to <body>
findings.evidence: Forced POST /api/bugs and PUT /api/bugs/:id to 500 with page.route. Enter in Title, or Enter on Save, gives BODY after the error alert appears, in Chromium and Firefox (Create) and Chromium (Edit). The fields and Save are disabled while the request is pending, so the focused one blurs. The trap recovers: the next Tab lands on Close. A failed DELETE is fine: focus returns to Delete. quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/*/keyboard-path.log "FAILED SAVE", quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/edit-errors.txt.
findings.fix: Use readOnly plus aria-disabled on the fields and Save while saving (as LoginPage now does), or focus the first field or the error list when the error is set.

findings.title: At 320 px the Owner column is clipped and Chromium keyboard users cannot scroll to it
findings.requirement: WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard; 1.4.10 Reflow (tables may scroll in 2-D, but the scroll must be operable)
findings.evidence: At 320x640 the Bug table region shows x 17-303, but the table is 363 px wide and Owner sits at 281-380. Chromium: the region has tabIndex -1, Tabbing onto the Owner header leaves scrollLeft 0, and ArrowRight does nothing. The Owner cells hold no focusable content, so nothing brings them into view. Firefox scrolls to 77 when the header takes focus. quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/reflow-table.txt, quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/chromium/screenshots/10b-table-320-after-tab.png.
findings.fix: Add tabIndex={0} to the role="region" wrapper (it is already named) and a visible focus ring, so arrow keys scroll it. Optionally stack or hide the ID column below sm.

findings.title: Status region skips a repeated message and briefly announces a stale count
findings.evidence: Two consecutive edits of the same bug: the first sets "Bug saved. 1 open bug shown."; the second produces zero mutations of the status node because the string is identical, so there is nothing to announce. After delete and after closing a bug, the region first says "Bug deleted. 1 open bug shown." (the row is still counted), then "Bug deleted. No bugs matched." once the refetch lands. After create: "Bug created. 15 open bugs shown." then "Bug created. 24 ...". Both engines (quality-reports/2026-09-22T230611Z/evidence/a11y/*/keyboard-path.log). Whether a screen reader speaks one or both messages is unverified.
findings.fix: Set lastAction after fetchBugs resolves, and clear the region (or append a counter or zero-width change) before each new message so repeats re-announce.

findings.title: Accessibility suite has weak guards and leaves the new focus handling unguarded
findings.requirement: Run rules: weak assertions in the suite are findings; WCAG 2.4.3, 4.1.2, 1.4.3/1.4.11 coverage
findings.evidence: Weak: :41 checks only that Open is pressed at load, never that Closed becomes pressed and Open false. :33 counts role=row > 1, which passes with the header plus any one row, loading or empty. :62 presses Escape on a closed select. :72 drives Delete/Cancel with the mouse. Not guarded at all: confirm dialog initial focus on Cancel (a11y-07), focus after save, delete and Clear (a11y-06), the Edit and confirm Tab traps and Shift+Tab, status text after save and delete, focus after a failed save, contrast, reflow and forced colors. Everything runs in Chromium only, although the Firefox walk shows engine differences (a11y-25).
findings.repro: Read tests/accessibility/accessibility.spec.ts; compare with the checks in this report.
findings.fix: Add atomic tests for Closed aria-pressed, confirm-dialog initial focus, focus after save and delete, the Edit/confirm traps, and a computed-contrast check of the tokens; run the keyboard tests in Firefox too.

notTested: axe-core: @axe-core/playwright is not installed, so it was not run; no packages added

Real screen readers (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS): wording and timing of the status region (a11y-26), whether the h1 focus on load is announced, virtual-cursor containment given only aria-modal (no inert on the background), and whether role=alert errors are read
WebKit/Safari: the suite skips it, and Tab skips buttons by default
--project=firefox run of tests/accessibility: every test there skips non-Chromium, so it would prove nothing; the headless Firefox walk was used instead
Real browser zoom and real Windows High Contrast: viewports and forcedColors were emulated
Headed native <select> popups: Escape inside an open popup (a11y-19)
Speech input and mobile screen-reader gestures
